proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Writing the orbit of u_j as {u_{j1}, ..., u_{jn_j}}, take the pair W' inside W inside U of the finite-flat-over-almost-dense lemma. Since U = t(s^{-1} of the closure of W), some u_{ji} lies in the closure of W; as a generic point of an irreducible component of a locally Noetherian scheme it lies in W itself; by R-invariance of W the whole orbit of u_j lies in W. By the cohomology-of-schemes lemma on images of finite morphisms over affine bases in the Noetherian setting, it suffices to find an R-invariant affine open V' of W' containing u_1, ..., u_m, because the corresponding open V of W will be affine; hence replace (U, R, s, t, c) by the restriction to W', where s and t are finite locally free. By the properties maximal-points lemma one finds an affine open containing all orbit points (a locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated lemma), and the groupoids find-invariant-affine lemma concludes. (source lines 2859-2884)
